reading.rtitle: The Form Is Not the Need
paras: A job requisition usually arrives as a form: a title, a salary range, a start date and one short line that says urgent. The form is necessary, because the system needs it. But the form is not the need. Very often, the hiring manager fills in the title of the person who left, and nobody asks if the team still needs exactly that person.

An HR Business Partner who receives a requisition has one job before anything else: to understand the business need. That takes a conversation, not an email. The best conversations start with an open question, such as what is driving this request, or walk me through a normal week in your team. A question that only accepts yes or no, such as do you need this person, always gets the same answer.

Three subjects usually come out of a good conversation. The first is the workload: how much work there is, and how much of it is new. The second is the impact on the team if nobody comes: what stops, what slows down, and what the other people stop doing to cover it. The third is time. Some needs are real only in the short term, for a project or a peak in the year, and a temporary solution is enough.

At the end of the conversation, the HRBP often discovers that the request is different from the form. Sometimes it is a replacement, sometimes it is a new position, and sometimes the right answer is to move somebody who already knows the company instead of bringing in a person from outside. The form comes back complete, and this time it tells the true story.

items.situation: A manager sends a requisition with only a title and the word urgent.
tips: Thanks for this. Before I open it, can you tell me what is driving this request?

items.situation: He says: "I just need a person, quickly."
tips: I understand. Walk me through a normal week in your team.
walk me through + a concrete period.

items.situation: You want to know what the person does every day.
tips: What does the person in this role do every day?

items.situation: You want to know if somebody left.
tips: Is this a replacement, or is it a new position?

items.situation: You want to know the impact if nobody comes.
tips: What happens to the team if nobody comes in the short term?

items.situation: You want the answer in a polite, indirect way.
tips: Can you tell me how many people do this work today?
indirect question: subject before verb, no do.

listenings.text: Hello everyone, a quick note about job requisitions before the planning cycle starts. Every week I receive requisitions with a title, a salary range and the word urgent, and nothing else. That is not enough for the committee, and honestly, it is not enough for us. Before you send me a requisition, please talk to the hiring manager. I want three answers on every form. First, the business need: what is driving this request, in one or two sentences. Second, the workload: what the person does every week, and how much of that work is new. Third, time: is the need permanent, or is it only in the short term? If it is only in the short term, let's look into a temporary solution first. Thank you, and send me your questions.

Hi Camila, it's Diego, from collections. I'm sending you a job requisition today, and I know you are going to ask me questions, so here is some background. I know about the freeze, so this is for April. My team has six analysts, and the workload grows every month, because the dealers pay later and later. Nobody is leaving, so this is not a replacement. I need a new position, a second senior analyst, for the difficult cases. In the short term, two people from the team cover part of it, but then they stop doing their own work, and our reports arrive late. I filled in the form with the title and the salary range, but the job description is not ready yet. Can we talk tomorrow morning? Thanks.
